gloss: to go overboard; to cut loose; to get carried away

definitions.gloss: to go overboard; to cut loose; to get carried away; to go too far
definitions.explanation: To lose self-control and behave excessively, especially in the context of having fun or celebrating. Implies going beyond reasonable limits.

examples.japanese: {飲|の}みすぎて{羽目|はめ}を{外|はず}した。
examples.english: I drank too much and got carried away.

examples.japanese: {久|ひさ}しぶりの{休|やす}みで{羽目|はめ}を{外|はず}してしまった。
examples.english: I went overboard since it was my first day off in a long time.

examples.japanese: {楽|たの}しむのはいいけど、{羽目|はめ}を{外|はず}さないようにね。
examples.english: It's fine to have fun, but don't go overboard, okay?

notes:
ETYMOLOGY:
{羽目|はめ} originally refers to the bit placed in a horse's mouth for control. To {外|はず}す (remove) it means the horse runs wild — hence, to lose restraint.

USAGE:
Most commonly used about drinking and partying. Usually implies that the person was having fun but went too far. Can be used self-deprecatingly or as a warning to others.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {羽目|はめ}を{外|はず}しすぎる (to go way too far)
- {羽目|はめ}を{外|はず}さないように (so as not to go overboard)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {調子|ちょうし}に{乗|の}る: to get carried away, to push one's luck — emphasis on getting overconfident
- やりすぎる: to overdo it — more direct and general
